combinations.readout: RhoA activation in CSPG-stimulated DRG lysates
combinations.magnitude: ibuprofen 11 AU vs control 76 AU; GW9662 alone 73 AU; with ibuprofen 88 AU
combinations.evidence_quote: The presence of GW9662 maintained RhoA activation (Fig. 3C: 73 ± 21 AU; Fig. 3D: 92 ± 31 AU), and significantly blocked RhoA inactivation when supplemented with ibuprofen/indomethacin (Fig. 3C: 88 ± 24 AU; Fig. 3D: 71 ± 43 AU) or GW1929 (Fig. 3C: 62 ± 15 AU; Fig. 3D: 69 ± 32 AU, p < 0.01).

combinations.magnitude: combination 89 μm avg/112 μm max vs control 274/317 μm; ibuprofen alone 726/837 μm; GW9662 alone 83/99 μm
combinations.evidence_quote: Additionally, the presence of GW9662 (83 ± 44 μm, 99 ± 63 μm) alone, and in combination with ibuprofen (89 ± 20 μm, 112 ± 19 μm) or GW1929 (32 ± 16 μm, 32 ± 16 μm) significantly reduced axonal growth (p < 0.001) compared to control cultures (274 ± 18 μm, 317 ± 24 μm) or cultures treated with vehicle (240 ± 37 μm, 280 ± 66 μm, p < 0.01).

combinations.readout: axonal growth (average and maximum axon length) from DRG explants

combinations.evidence_quote: Quantitative analysis revealed that indomethacin (614 ± 104 μm, 736 ± 41 μm) and GW1929 (609 ± 82 μm, 727 ± 53 μm) significantly enhanced (p < 0.01) axonal length while GW9662 (63 ± 26 μm, 63 ± 26 μm) significantly decreased (p < 0.001) axonal growth regardless of the presence of indomethacin (98 ± 11 μm, 98 ± 11 μm) or GW1929 (32 ± 31 μm, 32 ± 31 μm).
